RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT. Full text: org/missions/D9/IRPT/IRPT_BCKEND/deliverables/0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~V/the-export-role-reads-the-receipt.result.md blob d5a7ea87fd095cbdb6bb2a8e7cf6ae8dad3b7e58 @ea7d6eae26, section 5.
1. THE CLASS OF THE DEFECT: a Rule 24(i) FORWARD-LIST defect at infra/aws/lambda/investor-reporting/export/entry.py:100-103 @53fa406bf4 -- exc.__class__.__name__ in ('NoSuchKey','ClientError') enumerates two names its author had in mind instead of subtracting from what the call can raise. botocore 1.43.0 mints a MODELED class per error code (AccessDenied->AccessDenied, NoSuchKey->NoSuchKey, NoSuchBucket->NoSuchBucket, KMS.AccessDeniedException->ClientError), so 3 of the 4 codes this route can receive produce a name the list does not carry, and the one it catches is caught by accident of not being modeled. The remedy is NOT one more name: decide on the error CODE (exc.response['Error']['Code']) or on isinstance(exc, ClientError). WHAT THE BOUNDARY MUST CARRY: a role-plane failure must arrive as a NAMED refusal with its action and resource, impossible today because the recorder's sink is None (S91) -- so the mapping fix and the sink fix are TWO remedies and neither moves the other.
2. WAS THE KEY EVER INSIDE THE POLICY'S DECLARED REACH: NO, and they never overlapped at any vintage. core/layout.json @53fa406bf4 (terraform-generated; its _meta says IB-s-5 binds the per-firm IAM conditions to it) declares 3 families, all firms/{firm_id}/..., and _keys/keys.py:109-113 @53fa406bf4 holds the same 3 cross-checked by verify_against_layout(). entry.py:63-64 @53fa406bf4 is a FREE-TYPED string literal with an env override (IRPT_EXPORT_RECEIPT_KEY) Terraform never sets, while the route's own writer export/handler.py:126-130 @53fa406bf4 goes through keys.s3_evidence_key. THE DIVERGENCE IS THAT THE READER BYPASSED THE KEY BUILDER THE WRITER USES.
3. WHAT AN IAM GRANT'S ACCEPTANCE INSTRUMENT MUST DO: simulate-principal-policy false-ALLOWs on conditions it cannot evaluate AND false-DENIES on conditions it evaluates without context -- this seat hit the second half today and had carried 'kms:Decrypt implicitDeny' into the rtf-12 record; with --context-entries kms:ViaService the same call returns allowed. So it may never be the only evidence: exercise the real call as the real principal (the live invoke pair, which needs no assumable role), run the positive control as a SEPARATE invocation (mode 1 disarms an in-call control), and NAME the class and code received -- which on this estate requires the sink to exist. Today a grant on this route could be accepted only by the invoke pair, and the pair reports the served code but not the class.
